case_name: Jagadguru Annadanishwara Maha Swamiji v V.C.Allipur & Anr
facts: Appellant is before us, aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 31st May, 2007 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore in CCC No.341 of 2006 and also the order dated 11th June, 2007.
Respondent No.1 was working as an Assistant Teacher in a school run by the appellant.
In relation to his claim for promotion as a lecturer as he had obtained M.A. degree, he approached the school authorities.
Respondent No.1 then made a representation to the Deputy Director, Education who in turn asked the management to consider the case of the respondent No.1 for promotion.
The Director, Pre-University, Education passed an order on 25th July, 2005 in his favour.
Appellant preferred an appeal before the appropriate authority which is still pending.

Respondent No.1, however, filed an application purported to be under Sections 11 & 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 (for short 'the Act') before the Karnataka High Court praying, inter alia, for the following reliefs:
issues: Whether the Director of the Pre-University, Education is a Court within the meaning of the provisions of the Act or not.
petitioner_arguments: The Director of Pre-University, Education was not functioning as a Court within the provisions of the Act.
The impugned orders are wholly illegal.
The High Court had no jurisdiction to initiate any proceeding under the said Act.
respondent_arguments: The Director of Pre-University, Education is an authority created under a statute and not a Court.

By no stretch of imagination, it cannot be described as a Court so as to enable the first respondent to file an application for initiation of proceedings under the Contempt of Courts Act against the appellant herein.
court_reasoning: The Director of Pre-University, Education is not functioning as a Court within the provisions of the Act.
The impugned orders are wholly without jurisdiction and non est in the eyes of law and therefore are unsustainable.
holding: The Contempt Petition filed by the first respondent before the High Court is dismissed.
